blocks.heading: Parents on the Best Career

figures.label: Exam Candidate Count
figures.source: No. NEET 2026 had roughly 23 lakh candidates competing for about 1.1 lakh MBBS seats, and JEE Main pass rates for IIT/NIT seats sit under 4%. Most 12th-pass students in India were never going to get one of these seats by definition of the ratio alone. Strong, well-paid careers exist across commerce, design, healthcare-adjacent roles, government exams, skilled trades, and digital-skill paths that do not run through JEE or NEET at all.

visuals.alt: Decision checklist for Best Career for My Child.
visuals.caption: Questions to use before deciding.
visuals.heading: Questions Before Choosing

blocks.heading: One Core Skill That Matches the Target

items.text: One multiplier skill on top, communication, basic data or AI-tool fluency, or business sense, that makes the core skill more valuable.
Visible proof of work: a project, a portfolio piece, an internship result, or a small paid task a stranger can actually see.
Market positioning: knowing which employers or clients actually pay for this skill combination, not guessing.
Leading with "everyone in the family does X" instead of the child's actual fit.
Comparing your child to a cousin or neighbour's child who "settled down well."
Treating any hesitation about a "safe" field as ingratitude.
Bringing up money only as a threat, never as a shared planning exercise.
Deciding privately, then presenting it as the only real option.

blocks.heading: Tests Without Treating Them As a Verdict

items.text: Surface consistent interest and work-style patterns your child may not have named out loud.
Narrow a confusing list of 10-15 options down to a shortlist of 3-4.
Give the family a neutral third input, reducing pure opinion-based arguments.

blocks.heading: Conversation Families Avoid Until It's Too Late

items.text: Can your child name one specific target role this course leads to, not just "a good future".
Is the projected EMI realistic against the likely starting salary for that role, not the best-case one.
Does the family still have a buffer if the first job search after graduation takes longer than expected.
Has your child done any small project, internship, or proof of interest in this field already.
If the interest rate or fee structure changes, does the plan still hold.
World Economic Forum on how core job skills and entry-level hiring are shifting through 2030.
Wheebox India Skills Report on national employability and AI-driven hiring trends.
Government of India on NEP 2020's multidisciplinary and multiple entry-exit structure in higher education.
Peer-reviewed research on parental pressure, academic stress, and adolescent well-being around entrance exams in India.
National Education Policy 2020 official reference for structure and implementation timelines.
Government-recognised career and job services portal for India.
